title: CopyEscape Docker Flaw Lets Malicious Containers Overwrite Host Files and Execute Code
content_md: A newly disclosed Docker vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-17106, allows a malicious container to break out of the destination specified by docker cp and overwrite files on the host running the Docker CLI. The flaw does not automatically give a container unrestricted host control. Instead, it converts a copy-out operation into a host-side write primitive, operating with the permissions of the user or automation process that launches it. Imperva researchers identified the issue in Docker’s archive pipeline, and Docker lists it as a destination-escape flaw in the docker container cp command. CopyEscape Docker Flaw Docker cp does not directly transfer files between two filesystems. For a container-to-host copy, the daemon walks the requested container path, creates a tar archive, and sends that archive to the CLI for extraction. The container controls the archive’s source data, while the host-side CLI performs the filesystem operations. Security relies on two requirements: the archive must represent a consistent source filesystem, and the extractor must prevent every archive entry from resolving outside the destination. Docker Tar Extraction Flow (Source: Imperva) A process running in a malicious container can alter a pathname while Docker builds the archive. Ron Masas showed that Docker may first record a path as a directory, then observe it as a symbolic link when creating archive metadata.
